stem:
The diagram shows three everyday uses of a convex mirror: a scooter side-view mirror, a mirror at a sharp road bend, and a shop surveillance mirror.

Why is a convex mirror chosen for these uses?

options.text: It forms erect, smaller images and gives a wider field of view than a plane mirror.
It forms a magnified image so distant objects look larger than life.
Any curved mirror works the same, so a concave mirror would serve equally well here.
It is chosen only because the glass looks shiny, not because of image size or field of view.

teacher.key_rationale: Convex mirrors give erect, diminished images and a wide field of view, which suits side-view, road-bend, and surveillance uses. Magnified images and concave mirrors do not fit these uses; shininess alone is not the reason.
teacher.figure_note: Three panels: side-view, road bend, surveillance convex mirrors.
